title: Design System: Ravi Sweets — The Batch Card

display-xl.purpose: Page-defining headlines. Archivo at wdth 112. One per page at most.

display-lg.purpose: The hero h1 inside the batch card.

body.purpose: Running copy. Keep measures in the 48-70ch band.

label.purpose: The pre-printed caption on a form (.field-label). Archivo at wdth 84, always uppercase. The only small-caps label pattern on the site.

value.purpose: Courier Prime with tabular-nums (.field-value). Every batch number, date, weight, percentage and price. Never prose.

indic.purpose: Anek Telugu, variable 100-800, not preloaded. Short Telugu marks only, never body copy.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: The default. Most surfaces carry no shadow at all.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: A sheet resting on the ground. What .docket carries at rest.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hover response on an interactive sheet. Never a resting state.

shadows.name: stamp-contact
shadows.purpose: The hard contact edge under a .stamp. Collapses to 0 on :active as the stamp presses into the paper.

shadows.name: border-hairline
shadows.purpose: The 1px alpha-ink border (--color-border). 16% on the carbon register.

shadows.name: rule
shadows.purpose: The ruled line on a form (--color-rule) - heavier than a border, always horizontal. 30% on carbon.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions, register swaps and colour changes.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: Pressing a stamp: translateY(1px) with the contact shadow collapsing to zero.

motion.name: register-swap
motion.purpose: Body-level transition when the runtime palette changes.

motion.name: reveal-distance
motion.purpose: Entrance travel. Under prefers-reduced-motion, durations collapse to 0.01ms AND delays to 0s.

components.name: Stamp (Primary Action)
components.description: The primary action. A rubber stamp is rectangular and prints with a hard edge, so this is never a pill and never a gradient. Pressing it pushes it into the paper.
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 2px; background-color: var(--theme-accent, #2046C8); color: var(--theme-base, #E9EAE4); font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 92; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 22%, transparent); transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), box-shadow 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-stamp:hover { background-color: #16328F; } .ds-stamp:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-ring, #2046C8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-stamp:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 22%, transparent); }

components.name: Counterstamp (Secondary Action)
components.description: The secondary action: the outline, not the fill. A 1.5px inset ring rather than a border, so it does not shift layout against the filled stamp beside it.
components.css: .ds-stamp-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: var(--theme-accent, #2046C8); font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 92; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--theme-accent, #2046C8); transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-stamp-ghost:hover { background-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-accent, #2046C8) 8%, transparent); } .ds-stamp-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-ring, #2046C8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-stamp-ghost:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Docket (Card)
components.description: The only container in the system. A cut sheet of docket stock resting on the ground - 3px corners, a 1px alpha-ink border, and a contact shadow rather than a float. Replaced roughly 40 hand-built card variants.
components.html:
Qubani ka Meetha

Slow-cooked apricot, set overnight. Made without preservatives.
components.css: .ds-docket { background-color: var(--color-surface-elevated, #F6F7F3); color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(22,28,36,0.14)); border-radius: 3px; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: var(--font-body, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 6%, transparent), 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 7%, transparent); transition: box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-docket:hover { box-shadow: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 9%, transparent), 0 4px 10px color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 10%, transparent); } .ds-docket-title { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 112; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: -0.015em; margin: 0; } .ds-docket-body { margin: 0.375rem 0 0; font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); }

components.name: Docket with Perforated Edge
components.description: The world's signature: the perforated stub of a torn-off docket, rendered as a repeating radial gradient 8px in from the left edge. Reserved for the hero card and order receipts - it cheapens on repetition.
components.css: .ds-docket-perf { position: relative; background-color: var(--color-surface-elevated, #F6F7F3); color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(22,28,36,0.14)); border-radius: 3px; padding: 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.25rem 2.5rem; font-family: var(--font-body, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 6%, transparent), 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 7%, transparent); } .ds-docket-perf::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0.5rem; top: 0.5rem; bottom: 0.5rem; width: 3px; background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 1.5px 3px, var(--color-rule, rgba(22,28,36,0.26)) 0 1.5px, transparent 1.6px); background-size: 3px 9px; background-repeat: repeat-y; } .ds-perf-label { display: block; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 84; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); } .ds-perf-title { margin: 0.375rem 0 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Ruled Row (Label / Value)
components.description: The atom the whole system is built from: a pre-printed label left, a typed value right, separated by a full-width hairline. The last row's rule is removed. When in doubt about presenting a pair of facts, this is the answer.

components.css: .ds-field-list { margin: 0; } .ds-field-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(22,28,36,0.14)); } .ds-field-row:last-child { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-field-label { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 84; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); } .ds-field-value { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); } .ds-field-value--strong { font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Live Mark
components.description: "Made today" / "dispatching now". The only place ember appears. A 6px dot rather than a badge, deliberately: a grid of badges reads as a wall of colour, a grid of dots reads as a column of state.
components.css: .ds-live-mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 84; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-ember, #E2571F); } .ds-live-mark::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background-color: var(--color-ember, #E2571F); }

components.name: Section Head
components.description: One markup shape for every section heading on the site, replacing the duplicated eyebrow/h2/link cluster that was repeated across home, shop, category, festivals and corporate. Sits over a 2px rule with more space below the rule than above it.
components.html:
Also on the counter today

The whole catalogue →
components.css: .ds-docket-head { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; padding-bottom: 0.75rem; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; border-bottom: 2px solid var(--color-rule, rgba(22,28,36,0.26)); } .ds-head-label, .ds-head-link { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 84; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-head-label { color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); } .ds-head-link { color: var(--theme-accent, #2046C8); text-decoration: none; transition: color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-head-link:hover { color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); } .ds-head-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-ring, #2046C8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: A blank on the form. Docket-stock ground, 4px corners, hairline border. Focus shifts the border to the accent and adds a 2px ring at 30% - a border shift, never a glow.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.375rem; } .ds-field-caption { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 84; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); } .ds-input { background-color: var(--color-surface, #E9EAE4); color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, rgba(22,28,36,0.14)); border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.625rem 0.875rem; font-family: var(--font-body, 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-ink, #161C24) 40%, transparent); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--theme-accent, #2046C8); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-accent, #2046C8) 30%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: #dc2626; } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true']:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(220,38,38,0.3); }

Sale marks use ember and outrank bestseller marks.

text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-text-muted, #565F68); } .ds-product-price { margin: 0.125rem 0 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; components.name: Code Chip
components.description: The one sanctioned pill in the system. Promo codes and count badges only - a genuine chip, set in the mono because a code is a recorded value. A rubber stamp is rectangular, so reach for this rarely.
components.css: .ds-code-chip { display: inline-block; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; background-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--theme-glow, #EBC77E) 45%, transparent); color: var(--theme-ink, #161C24); font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }

narrative.overview:
The paperwork is the proof. The brand's binding claim is that the sweets are made without preservatives and dispatched the same day, and the thing that actually demonstrates that is the kitchen's own record: the docket taped above the kadai, the gummed label on the box, the rubber-stamped date, the FSSAI composition panel. So the record is not decoration around the interface - the record IS the interface. A visitor reads a batch number, a MADE date computed live, a BEST BEFORE four days out, and a PRESERVATIVES: NIL row, and believes the claim because they can read it rather than because a paragraph asserts it.

The world is defined as much by what it refuses. Every neighbouring Indian sweets brand ships the same arrangement: a warm cream ground, a heritage display serif, a festive saffron or rose accent, and freshness stated as a sentence. This system rejects all four. The ground is cool NCR docket stock, faintly green - so the food and the manila tag are the only warm things on any page, which is the entire appetite strategy. The display face is a grotesque, not a serif; authority here comes from the grid and the record, not from heritage lettering. The accent is a stamp-pad blue occupying hue ground no competitor holds. And freshness is a field on a form with a date in it.

Density is that of a working document, not a lookbook. Type is compact, rules are horizontal and structural, corners are guillotined, and elevation is a sheet in contact with a counter rather than a card floating over one. Colour is scarce and load-bearing: the accent is ink, the manila is a wash, and ember means one thing only. Warmth in this system comes from the photography and the manila tag - never from the paper.
keyCharacteristics: Cool docket stock ground (#E9EAE4), never cream, never pure white
Stamp-pad blue accent at hue 226, verified clear of the category
One grotesque family (Archivo) carrying hierarchy on its width axis; a typewriter mono (Courier Prime) carrying every recorded value
Square-cut paper: radii 0-8px; elevation caps at a 10px blur
Ruled label/value rows as the atom the whole system is built from
Two registers, one grammar: light docket and dark carbon copy swap roles without component changes
Ember reserved exclusively for live state
One container, one rhythm, one product grid

rules.name: The Runtime Palette Rule
rules.body: The live palette is resolved at RUNTIME by applyPalette() from the active row in the Supabase theme_presets table (supabase/migrations/0011_batch_card_world.sql seeds batch-card as active and carbon-copy as an inactive alternative). The :root values in globals.css are FIRST-PAINT DEFAULTS ONLY and are overwritten the moment the active preset loads. Changing a brand colour in code alone does nothing to the live site - it must land in the database too. Keep the :root block byte-identical to DOCKET in palette.ts so the first paint does not flash.

rules.name: The Ember Containment Rule
rules.body: #E2571F appears on .live-mark and on the sale flag, and nowhere else. It is excluded from RegisterTokens by construction and palette.test.ts asserts that no register token equals it. If you want a warm highlight, you want the manila label, not ember.

rules.name: The 25-Degree Rule
rules.body: The accent must clear all nine tracked competitor hues by at least 25 degrees. palette.test.ts enforces this against a measured set (Cadbury 2685C, Bombay Sweet Shop wine and petrol, Anand crimson and gold, Almond House terracotta, Haldiram burnt brick, Bikanervala vermilion, Sweet Karam teal) and separately pins the accent to the exact string #2046C8. Both tests must be re-run and re-argued before any accent change, not deleted.

rules.name: The Manila-Is-Ground Rule
rules.body: #EBC77E is a wash and a panel ground for ink. Never set text in it, never use it as an accent, never put accent-coloured text on it above UI scale - only accentDeep on manila is certified, and only at 3:1.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: The base never warms and never becomes #FFFFFF. The system is cool precisely so the food photography and the manila tag are the only warm elements on screen; warm the ground and the appetite contrast collapses.

rules.name: The Width-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy rides Archivo's wdth axis (84 / 92 / 112), not weight alone. That width range is why one family can do both the display and body jobs without a second face. Reaching for a heavier weight where a width change is available flattens the system back into a generic sans.

rules.name: The Typed-Value Rule
rules.body: Anything that was recorded - a batch number, a date, a weight, a percentage, a price - is set in Courier Prime with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Tabular is not optional: a column of prices that does not align is the exact failure this world exists to avoid. Conversely, prose is never set in the mono; it is a value face, not a texture.

rules.name: The One Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: .field-label is the only small-caps label pattern on the site. The audit that produced this world counted eleven hand-rolled variants of it. If a new surface needs a small tracked caption, it uses .field-label and does not re-declare text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[...].

rules.name: The One Container Rule
rules.body: Every storefront surface uses .container-site and nothing else. .container-wide is for the admin console and dense tables. A new page that introduces its own max-w-* is a regression, not a variation.

rules.name: The Two-Up Rule
rules.body: Two products per row at the smallest breakpoint is not negotiable. Products-per-viewport is the strongest lever on browse-to-detail conversion, and a food grid reads perfectly well two-up at 375px.

rules.name: The Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Section spacing comes from .section-y / .section-y-tight. If a surface needs different air, change the class definition once - do not write py-24 on the section.

rules.name: The Contact-Not-Float Rule
rules.body: Every shadow leads with a 0 1px 0 contact edge before any blur, and no blur exceeds 10px. If a surface needs to feel more present, raise its tone or give it a rule - do not raise its shadow.

rules.name: The Motion-As-Response Rule
rules.body: Elevation changes are responses to state, never decoration. .docket moves soft to lifted on hover in 200ms; .stamp presses in 120ms. Motion easing is cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) (standard) or cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (emphasised), with durations from the 100-650ms scale. Entrance reveals travel 12px. Under prefers-reduced-motion all durations collapse to 0.01ms AND all delays to 0s - a backwards-filled entrance would otherwise hold its hidden state and then pop.

rules.name: The Square-Cut Rule
rules.body: New surfaces use rounded-lg (3px) or less. Anything above rounded-3xl (8px) is out of world. rounded-full on a rectangular element is always wrong.

rules.name: The Perf-Edge Rule
rules.body: .docket--perf is the world's signature and it cheapens on repetition. It belongs on the hero card and on order receipts. It currently appears on exactly one element and should stay in the low single digits.

dos: Do ship palette changes as a Supabase migration against theme_presets, not as a code edit. Code-only changes affect first paint and nothing else.
Do keep the :root block in globals.css byte-identical to DOCKET in palette.ts, so first paint does not flash into the runtime palette.

Do run `vitest run src/lib/theme/palette.test.ts` after any colour change. 48 assertions currently pass; they pin every contrast pair, the exact accent hex, the 25-degree competitor clearance, ember's exclusion from the register set, and the five-member product palette list.
Do reach for .docket, .field-row, .field-label, .field-value, .stamp, .docket-head before writing new component CSS. A new surface needing a container uses .docket.
Do set every recorded value in Courier Prime with tabular-nums.
Do use data-register="carbon" to take a subtree dark. It re-themes everything inside with zero component changes.
Do use #6B737B (steel hairline) for any rule that carries meaning; #8A9099 (steel rule) does not clear 3:1.
Do mirror any edit to PRODUCT_PALETTES into packages/shared/src/catalogue/palettes.ts - the set is deliberately duplicated because the shared package cannot import upward.
donts: Don't warm the ground or move it toward #FFFFFF. The cool stock is the appetite strategy.
Don't use ember for anything but live state. It is outside the register token set specifically so it cannot spread, and a test asserts that.
Don't set text in the manila label colour, or put accent text on a manila panel above UI scale.
Don't introduce a display serif, a new font family, or a heavier weight where an Archivo wdth change would do.
Don't write rounded-full on a rectangular element, or arbitrary radii like rounded-[2rem]. Both escape the compressed scale.
Don't add a max-w-* to a page. Use .container-site.
Don't write ad-hoc py-* on a section. Use .section-y / .section-y-tight.
Don't hand-roll another eyebrow (text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[...]). Use .field-label.
Don't repeat .docket--perf. It is the signature and it cheapens on repetition.
Don't exceed a 10px shadow blur or add a hover lift to a stamp.
Don't move the accent hue without re-running the clearance test and arguing the result. Deleting the test is not passing it.
Don't re-add cream, anjeer, pista or gunmetal to the Tailwind palette. They were removed for having zero class usages; register colour is read through the --theme-* / --color-* properties instead.

Don't use hex-valued CSS variables in Tailwind colour bindings. They must be rgb(var(--x-rgb) / <alpha-value>) - with a hex-valued var, text-theme-ink/60 silently emits nothing, which is how 1003 opacity usages were once dead across the tree.
